title: "What if my job doesn't have metrics?" (and what to do)
description:
Metrics are one of the BEST ways to show impact on a resume, but what if you don’t have access to the numbers from your company? Here are three tips to get you headed in the right direction, and if you haven’t asked your supervisor for the numbers it doesn’t hurt to try. #resumetips #resumeadvice #resumetok #resumemistakes #resumehelp #jobseeker #jobseekers

transcript: If you're having trouble putting metrics on your resume to show impact because you don't know the exact numbers, here's a few tips. The first thing is just to not use exact numbers. If you use percentages, you can more roughly estimate the number. The second is to change the timetable for that metric. Maybe you don't know year-over-year performance, maybe it's just month-over-month or week-over-week or even just like a single day instance where you can apply that metric to. Then the third is to change from a company level metric to a personal level metric. Maybe you have no idea about the numbers and no one's going to tell you. That's frustrating but fair. But you do know how long it took you to complete projects when you first started your job. What about now? Did you get faster? That efficiency is a personal metric. Definitely a tricky subject. So, I'm live right now if you want to talk.
